page.layout: One block of verse in a single column, centred under the running head; a page number at the top right; a small ornament (cross, circle and 4) below the verse. No notes in the margins.

main_text.p: Promissa tam solere te[?] Praestare liberaliter.
Vt qui fidem semel datam Ipsis tibi rebellibus, Ipsa cruentus in cruce Plene volens persoluueris.
Sed interista, ne, rogo, Tot obrutum me fluctibus, Anima quoque ipsa naufragum Totum sinas submergier.
Animam sed istam corporis Mors ipsa sursum transferat. Degustet illic vt noua Parata vita munera.
His dum reuinctis denuo Semel relicto puluere, Aeterna tecum gaudeam Certa quietis gaudia.

page.notes: Printed text is in Latin verse, with the printer's long s and italic type rendered as in the scan. Several words are doubtful at the edge of the damaged paper: "solere" [?] and "Promissa" [?] in the first line, and "interista" [?] in the second stanza. The stanza line "Plene volens" and "Ipsa cruentus" are read as printed. The mark at the foot is a printed ornament, not text.
